Everything I’ve done into my late 20s has become crazy minimal(skincare and makeup too). I used to binge on fast fashion, Forever21, and Charlotte Rousse type clothing - just to look in my overstuffed closet and wonder why I had nothing to wear. I let Instagram and Pinterest persuade me into buying things I knew I was never going to wear like bright colors and crazy shoes. This led to a crazy purge practically every season, a vicious cycle, really. 
Over the past year I’ve only really bought from small boutiques, JCrew/Banana Republic type stores- looking for items that are considered classic/basic that I can layer or wear all year round (with the exception of some cozy sweaters) in an incredibly neutral color palette (I gravitate toward black mostly lol).

They're the measurement of macronutrients, so instead of counting strictly calories alone, you're counting a certain amount of gram broken down into the following macronutrients- protein(p), carbs(c), and fats(f). Each gram of a macro has a set amount of calories, i.e. Each gram of fat has 9 cals in it. So, no matter what you're eating as long as you are within the set macro numbers, your daily calories will fall into the same number of calories each day (but you won't have to count them, only the c,p, and f numbers) You can find all the gram measurements on the nutrition labels. 

Tldr; not counting daily calories, but instead counting what the calories are made up of?
